styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Souq lanes, the Grand Mosque and Bahrain's pearling past.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Fort, museums and the old capital at Muharraq.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Souq snacks, Bahraini rice dishes and café culture.

stays.why: Walk to the souq, Bab Al Bahrain and the waterfront. Cheapest base and the most local feel.
Modern malls, cinemas and cafés. Good for families and shoppers; a short taxi to the old town.
Restaurants, bars and mid-range hotels. Popular with nightlife and long-stay visitors.
Quiet, upscale and close to the National Museum and the corniche. Business-hotel comfort.

food: Try Bahraini dishes: machboos (spiced rice with meat or fish), muhammar (sweet rice) and balaleet.
Manama Souq is the place for cheap eats: shawarma, samboosas and fresh juice for a few dinars.
Look for a traditional Bahraini breakfast of eggs, bread and halwa; ask your hotel for a local spot.
Seafood is good value here. Grilled hammour and prawns are common on menus.
Alcohol is served in licensed hotel bars and restaurants only. Dress modestly in the souq and mosques.
more_time: Cross to Muharraq for the old houses, the pearling path and a quieter feel than central Manama.
Take a day trip to the Bahrain Fort (Qal'at al-Bahrain) and its site museum; check opening hours on the day.
Spend an afternoon at the National Museum, then walk the corniche at sunset.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the souq, the fort and the museums at an easy pace; add a night for Muharraq and a beach afternoon.

month_notes: January: mild days around 20°C and cool nights. The best month for walking the souq.
February: still mild, a few rain days. Carry a light jacket for evenings.
March: warming to 25°C. Comfortable for sightseeing and outdoor cafés.
April: hot at 30°C by day. Do outdoor sights in the morning.
May: 34°C and dry. Plan indoor stops and drink plenty of water.
June: very hot at 37°C. Keep to air-conditioned malls and museums at midday.
July: the hottest month, 39°C. Go out early or after sunset only.
August: as hot as July, 39°C. Expect humid evenings by the water.
September: still 37°C. Slightly better late in the month.
October: cooling to 33°C. Good again for the fort and corniche walks.
November: pleasant at 28°C. A strong month for the old town.
December: mild at 22°C with a few rain days. Busy and comfortable.

climate_guide.summary: Hot desert climate: long, very hot summers, mild winters and almost no rain.

items.title: Best time: November to March
items.text: Days around 20–28°C and cooler evenings. Ideal for the souq, the fort and walking.

items.title: Summer is extreme (June to September)
items.text: Highs of 37–39°C. Stay indoors at midday and go out early or after dark.

items.title: Humid by the water
items.text: Muggy evenings from May to October, especially along the corniche.

items.title: Almost no rain
items.text: A few short showers between December and March. No umbrella needed most of the year.

items.title: Dusty winds
items.text: Occasional sand haze in spring and early summer can dull the sky.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light breathable clothes, a hat and sunscreen; a light layer for winter nights and indoor AC; modest clothing for mosques.

transit.best: Buses for cheap trips, ride apps or taxis for speed; rent a car if you plan to explore the island.

modes.text: No metro or tram. Don't plan around rail inside the city.

Bahrain Public Transport runs routes across the city; route A1 links the airport and Manama every 20 minutes. Single fare 300 fils paper, or 250 fils with a Go Card; daily cap 600 fils. Weekly pass BD 3 and 28-day pass BD 12 need a personalised Go Card from a terminal office.
Taxis are metered but pricey; airport rides add BD 2 and hotel pickups add BD 1. Uber and Careem work in Bahrain.
Renting a car is cheaper than relying on taxis for a full day of sightseeing.
Fine in the souq and old town in the cooler months. Use a bus or taxi for longer hops in summer.
